convoLines.text: "What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Alright — I should get back to it."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"Still on what you think happened to us."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Silas owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Sleep's gone strange. I sleep with one ear uncovered, always at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Keisha grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Maya is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
You show them Blackberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I can't read, and I'm scared it matters now."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Xavier shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"I needed someone to know — just one person. Thank you for being that person. Good talking."
"What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about?"
"Take your time."
"Still on that question."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Still on where you're from."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Maya doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Silas is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Maya is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
You show them Feral Rice — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«ሄይ... አማርኛ ትችላለህ? አይ? ...ውይ።»
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." My digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+909 kcal to the pantry.)
«ትክክል።» They nod back, a little quicker this time.
«ይህንን ውለታ አልረሳም።» (you catch 'ውለታ' — favor, 'አልረሳም' — won't forget) A smile, tired but real.
«በጣም ጥሩ ሰው ነዎት።» (you catch 'ጥሩ' — good) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You lean in, catching the rise and fall of it. «ተረድተሃል?» (you catch 'ተረድተሃል' — understood)
My laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — አዎ፣ እኔም እንደዛው እሰማለሁ።" They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
They hear you out, but something in them stays guarded.
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful. — ask anyone!"
"Still on whether you're angry."
"What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon. Just... be straight with me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Hardened Calorie Run. They just... took Keisha and Xavier. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Anyway." A small smile.
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Maya is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
«እዚህ በመሆኑ ደስ ብሎኛል። በእርግጥ።» (you catch 'ደስ' — glad)
You walk to the tree line with My. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
«አዎ፣ ልክ እንደዛ ነው።» (Yes, it's exactly like that. — you're fairly sure) They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
«እዚህ ስላለህ አመሰግናለሁ።» (Thank you for being here. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.

«ሁሉም ነገር ደህና ይሆናል።» (Everything will be well. — you're fairly sure) You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it. "Food?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «አንተ... እዚህ አለቃ ነህ?» (Are you... the boss here? — you're fairly sure)
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Water's almost gone — 2 liters. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 2 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You saw it too, right? Hardened Calorie Run. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Maya nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't."
"All right. Show me when we work together."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? At night I talk to someone who isn't there anymore."
They grin when they spot you — unguarded, for once.
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there."
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
"Take your time."
"Let me be straight — Still on that question."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together. Worth considering."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"

"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The whole fire was arguing about The Focus Group last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Bastard' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
They nod, giving you room to think.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You offered to show me while we work. I'd still like to learn, when there's time."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
The moment passes without landing. Not yet.
"Okay, I'm all ears."
"The cistern's nearly dry — 4 liters left. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"4 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
As I said — Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Xavier is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that water haul."
"This was good." They mean it.

giftSample: You notice the village gives you room on the path now. Not fear, exactly. Room.
💛 You hold Contract Quill. It has signed three leases, two loans, and one terrible contract you still regret. The penmanship was always excellent. The judgment, less so. Your gifts are not mastered —
🍽️ Jorge looks at the full shelves and waves off the day's share. "No more into the store — we eat at the fire, and the shelves keep."
rumorSample: Riders on the ridge — no, a cart. A TRADER. Word travels: Haven has food, and where there's food there's trade.

"Earned, not given. You did the work — we just wrote it down."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Silas Ross is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Silas Ross is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Silas kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Silas's gone." Maya looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Silas." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Penelope blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Scrounger (Level 1). Ruin looting finds +1 item.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Ritual & Meaning (Level 1). Marking the dead matters. Even without religion, ritual holds grief.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Light Fingers (Level 1). Steal from pantry without trust loss (50%). If caught, -20 trust.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Grave Robber (Level 1). You can loot the dead (villagers, monsters). Good gear. -15 trust if seen.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Field Dressing (Level 1). Break down game fast and clean. Less waste, more meat, usable parts.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Silas Ross, 41 days. The mantle passes to Penelope Han.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Penelope Han, 50 — a street artist. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Silas — and Silas is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Keisha, Maya, My and 5 more speak for Penelope — "Silas trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Penelope before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
d81: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Penelope Han is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d81: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d81: 🕯️ Penelope is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.
d81: 🕯️ Penelope Han is dead — betrayal. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d81: What Penelope kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d81: No one is left to pick up the Codex. The village dies out — quietly, the way villages do. The season ends here.
